_doc: Revert-verify mutants for #4369 (TripleClassHierarchy.isSubClassOf memo). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py packages/cli/tests/unit/commands/triple-class-hierarchy-memo-4369.spec.json after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute; the driver copies the tree with node_modules symlinked, splices one mutation into the copy's validate-schema.ts and runs the validate-schema unit suite; `expect` names the axes that MUST go red). Axis keys are the H<N> prefixes of the it() titles — `red_re` reads them, so they stay unique inside this file.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/validate-schema.ts

M1_memo_never_hits._note: Every lookup misses, so the walk runs on every call and the memo is inert. The write path is untouched, so the verdicts stay correct — only the walk-count axes can see this.

M2_positive_only_memo._note: The naive shape the issue warns about: `if (cached)` stores hits and leaves the EXHAUSTIVE false-verdict walk recomputing. H1 stays green under it by construction — that is why H2 exists separately.

M3_lookup_ignores_the_parent._note: Child-keyed memo: the first verdict cached for a child answers every later parent of that child. H6 joins the set because its cyclic fixture asks several parents of the same child.

M4_verdict_inverted_before_caching._note: Guards H3 against being written as a self-consistency check: a memo that inverts answers consistently, so only ABSOLUTE expectations catch it. H1/H2 are in the measured set too — they redden on their VALUE assertion (`toBe(true)` / `toBe(false)`), which runs before their walk-count assertion, not because they observe the memo.
